n2-set-5-q-1.translation: Because of my parents' financial circumstances, I changed my plans to attend a vocational school.
n2-set-5-q-1.correctAnswerEnglish: henkou / 変更 - change or alteration

choices.reason: Hengou voices the second kanji as gou; 更 is kou in 変更.
Henka is 変化, a different word meaning change or transformation.
Henkou is the reading of 変更; 進路を変更する means to change one's course or plans.
Henkan is 変換, meaning conversion, not the reading of 変更.

n2-set-5-q-2.translation: Hopes grew that the team would win its first Olympic medal in this event.
n2-set-5-q-2.correctAnswerEnglish: fukuranda / 膨らんだ - swelled or grew

choices.reason: Karanda suggests 絡んだ, meaning became entangled; it is not 膨らんだ.
Fukuranda is the past form of 膨らむ; expectations can figuratively swell or grow.
Niranda suggests 睨んだ, meaning glared or estimated, not swelled.
Haranda suggests 孕んだ, meaning conceived or contained, not the reading of 膨らんだ.

n2-set-5-q-3.translation: The course popular with students is Introduction to Economics.
n2-set-5-q-3.correctAnswerEnglish: gairon / 概論 - an introductory survey or overview

choices.reason: Kiron does not read 概論; 概 is pronounced gai in this compound.
Shoron would point to a different first kanji and is not the reading of 概論.
Gairon is the standard reading of 概論, an overview of a subject.
Jiron does not read 概論; neither kanji has that reading here.

n2-set-5-q-4.translation: My aim in climbing mountains is not to stand at the summit, but to take my time enjoying nature.
n2-set-5-q-4.correctAnswerEnglish: choujou / 頂上 - summit or top

choices.reason: Toujou is not the reading of 頂上; the first kanji is chou here.
Choujou is the standard reading of 頂上, the top of a mountain.
Koujou is another sound and can represent words such as 向上, improvement.
Teijou does not read 頂上; 頂 is not tei in this compound.

n2-set-5-q-5.translation: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government announced a new system aimed at raising standards of medical care.
n2-set-5-q-5.correctAnswerEnglish: suijun / 水準 - standard or level

choices.reason: Zuijun voices 水 as zui; 水 is sui in 水準.
Suijun is the reading of 水準; 医療水準 means the level of medical care.
Suishun changes 準 from jun to shun, which is not its reading here.
Zuishun changes both sui to zui and jun to shun.

n2-set-5-q-6.translation: Causing people in a vulnerable position mental or physical suffering is called power harassment.
n2-set-5-q-6.correctAnswerEnglish: kutsuu / 苦痛 - pain or suffering

choices.reason: 苦痛 combines hardship and pain; it names the mental and physical suffering in the sentence.
苦通 uses 通, passage or communication, instead of 痛, pain.
具 means a tool or equipment; 具痛 is not the spelling of kutsuu.
悲痛 means deep grief and is read hitsuu, not kutsuu.

n2-set-5-q-7.translation: This morning it was so cold that my hands froze and I could hardly grasp anything.
n2-set-5-q-7.correctAnswerEnglish: kogoete / 凍えて - numbed or frozen by cold

choices.reason: 冷えて means cooled down, but the printed kogoete is written with 凍 and implies freezing.
寒えて is not the standard spelling of kogoete; 寒い is an adjective.
凍えて is the te-form of 凍える, to freeze or become numb with cold.
涼 means pleasantly cool; 涼えて does not write the freezing-cold verb kogoete.

n2-set-5-q-8.translation: Because we knew the opposing team's weakness, we were able to gain an advantage in the match.
n2-set-5-q-8.correctAnswerEnglish: nigitte / 握って - held or had a firm grasp of

choices.reason: 挟 means to pinch or put between; it does not write nigiru here.
握って is the te-form of 握る; 弱点を握る means to know or hold an opponent's weakness.
担 means to carry or shoulder; 担って is ninatte, not nigitte.
捕 means to catch; 捕って is not the kanji for grasping a weakness.

n2-set-5-q-9.translation: Our interests aligned with those of the business partner, and the contract negotiations came together.
n2-set-5-q-9.correctAnswerEnglish: rigai / 利害 - interests, gains and losses

choices.reason: 理外 uses 理, reason, and 外, outside; it does not mean mutual interests.
理害 replaces 利, benefit, with 理 and is not the word rigai.
利外 replaces 害, harm or loss, with 外 and is not the established compound.
利害 pairs benefits and losses; 利害が一致する means interests coincide.

n2-set-5-q-10.translation: After piling up tough training sessions, I was finally able to overcome my weaknesses.

choices.reason: 克服 means to overcome; 欠点を克服する means to overcome a weakness.
告 means to announce; 告服 is not the word for overcoming a weakness.
降服 suggests surrendering, the opposite direction of overcoming a weakness.
攻 means to attack; 攻服 is not the established spelling of kokufuku.

n2-set-5-q-11.translation: This task is not physically demanding work, so it is suitable for older people.
n2-set-5-q-11.correctAnswerEnglish: 力仕事 - physical or manual labor

choices.reason: 力仕事 means work requiring physical strength; the sentence says this task is not that.
重仕事 is not the established compound for physical labor; 重 describes heaviness.
諸仕事 is not the phrase for strenuous work; 諸 means various.
全仕事 would mean all work, not labor requiring physical strength.

n2-set-5-q-12.translation: We somehow managed to keep the drinking party within a budget of 3,000 yen per person.

choices.reason: 予算中 does not express staying within a budget; 中 means middle or during.
予算下 is not the normal compound for a cost remaining within the budget.
予算外 means outside or beyond the budget, the opposite of おさまった here.
予算内 means within the budget; 予算内におさまる is the natural collocation.

n2-set-5-q-13.translation: He is an influential person in the town.

choices.reason: 有力家 is not the usual noun for an influential individual; 家 marks certain specialists.
有力者 is the established compound for an influential person or power broker.
有力人 is not the idiomatic person noun; 者 is used here, not 人.
有力民 is not a word for a town's influential resident; 民 means people collectively.

n2-set-5-q-14.translation: This is merely my opinion as a private individual.

choices.reason: 単個人 is not the idiomatic phrase for speaking in one's personal capacity.
各個人 means each individual, but 各個人として would not identify this speaker's own view.
唯個人 is not the established expression for an individual's private opinion.
一個人として means as one individual, separate from any official role.

n2-set-5-q-15.translation: Since I became ill, my outlook on life has changed.
n2-set-5-q-15.correctAnswerEnglish: 人生観 - view of life or outlook on life

choices.reason: 人生感 is not the established compound for a philosophy or outlook on life.
人生考 is not the word for one's outlook; 考 means thought or consideration.
人生観 means view of life; illness changed how the speaker sees life.
人生想 is not the established expression for a worldview.

n2-set-5-q-16.translation: Eastern medicine places particular importance on the feet, which support the whole body.
n2-set-5-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: 重要視する - to regard as important

choices.reason: 大事 means important, but 大事視 is not the usual compound with 視.
優先 means priority; 優先視 is not the collocation used for valuing the feet.
貴重 means precious; 貴重視 is not the established phrase here.
重要視する means to attach importance to something; it fits 足を特に...視する.

n2-set-5-q-17.translation: The heat expelled by air conditioners makes it even hotter outside.
n2-set-5-q-17.correctAnswerEnglish: 増大させる - to increase or intensify

choices.reason: 増大させる can intensify a degree such as outdoor heat.
急増 describes a rapid increase in amount or number, not usually a degree of heat.
増減 means increase and decrease; the sentence describes only making heat worse.
激増 describes a dramatic increase in quantity, not the intensity of the heat here.

n2-set-5-q-18.translation: You're not a child anymore, so decide for yourself without having to be told every single thing.
n2-set-5-q-18.correctAnswerEnglish: いちいち - every single time or in every detail

choices.reason: あちこち means here and there, referring to places rather than repeated instructions.
まあまあ means so-so or reasonably; it cannot modify 言われなくても in this sense.
いちいち言われる means to be told each little thing; the speaker wants independent judgment.
それぞれ means each or respectively, not being told each detail.

n2-set-5-q-19.translation: I think one reason this product does not sell is that its packaging design is too ordinary.
n2-set-5-q-19.correctAnswerEnglish: パッケージ - package or packaging

choices.reason: パート means part or part-time work, not a product's outer package.
パーソナル means personal, which does not name the item's designed wrapper.
パターン means pattern; the sentence specifies the design of the product's packaging.
パッケージ is the package; パッケージのデザイン is packaging design.

n2-set-5-q-20.translation: For work-related worries, I think it is best to consult a helpful supervisor at work.
n2-set-5-q-20.correctAnswerEnglish: 面倒見のよい - caring, helpful, or attentive

choices.reason: 面倒見のよい describes someone who looks after others and gives useful help.
世話見 is not the established phrase; 世話をする means to care for someone.
加減見 is not a phrase describing a supportive supervisor; 加減 is degree or adjustment.
手数見 is not the collocation; 手数 means effort or trouble.

n2-set-5-q-21.translation: He has earned a doctorate and is getting married, so happy occasions keep coming his way.
n2-set-5-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: おめでたいこと - happy or congratulatory events

choices.reason: かしこい means clever; a doctorate and marriage are events to celebrate, not clever events.
ふさわしい means suitable, but this does not convey the celebratory tone of both events.
おめでたい describes occasions worthy of congratulations, such as graduation and marriage.
したしい means close or familiar and does not describe congratulatory events.

n2-set-5-q-22.translation: If you feel a little tired, it is good to eat foods containing plenty of vitamin C.

choices.reason: 包む means to wrap something; it does not state a food's nutrient content.
含む means to contain; ビタミンCを多く含む食品 is food rich in vitamin C.
帯びる means to carry or take on a quality; it is not the ordinary verb for nutrients in food.
握る means to grasp with the hand, not to contain a vitamin.

n2-set-5-q-23.translation: The hiking trip was canceled because of rain.
n2-set-5-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: 流れた - was called off or canceled

choices.reason: 延期になった means postponed to a later date; 流れた does not promise a new date.
中止になった means canceled; that is what 流れた means for an event.
見直された means reviewed or reconsidered, not canceled by rain.
変更になった means changed; it is broader than the trip being called off.

n2-set-5-q-24.translation: The sky suddenly darkened, and large raindrops began to fall.
n2-set-5-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: にわかに - suddenly or abruptly

choices.reason: すっかり means completely; it describes degree, not the sudden onset of rain.
ぼんやり means vaguely or dimly, not abruptly.
くっきり means clearly or sharply outlined, not suddenly.
いきなり means suddenly and matches にわかに in the changing sky.

n2-set-5-q-25.translation: She always looks at the world with a detached, cool-headed eye.
n2-set-5-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: 覚めた目 - a detached or dispassionate gaze

choices.reason: 冷静な means calm and objective; it matches the detached attitude of 覚めた目.
鋭い means sharp or perceptive; sharp insight is not the same as emotional detachment.
確かな means certain or reliable, not emotionally detached.
温かい means warm or sympathetic, the opposite tone from 覚めた目.

n2-set-5-q-26.translation: A friend forcibly took me to the party.

choices.reason: むりやり means by force or against someone's wishes; it matches 強引に.
こっそり means secretly, which does not convey pressure on the speaker.
しきりに means repeatedly or eagerly, not forcibly.
わざわざ means taking the trouble to do something, not coercion.

n2-set-5-q-27.translation: My senior colleague helps support my work.
n2-set-5-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: サポートして - supporting or helping

choices.reason: 理解して means understanding the work, not actively supporting it.
評価して means evaluating the work, not helping with it.
応援して means supporting or backing someone; it is closest to サポートして.
仕上げて means finishing the work, which is a different action.

n2-set-5-q-28.translation: Choose the correct use of compression: Putting a futon in a bag and removing the air compresses it until it is thin.

choices.reason: Moving to reduce commuting time calls for 短縮, shortening time, not physical 圧縮.
Reducing the number of employees calls for 削減, a cut in staffing, not 圧縮 here.
Removing air from a bag compresses the futon physically; 薄く圧縮できる is natural.
Shortening a skirt by three centimeters calls for 丈を詰める, not 圧縮.

n2-set-5-q-29.translation: Choose the correct use of boro: She acts refined, but sooner or later she will reveal her true flaws.
n2-set-5-q-29.correctAnswerEnglish: ぼろを出す - to reveal one's flaws or true colors

choices.reason: A name that sounds good has 語呂がいい; ぼろ is not pleasing sound or rhythm.
ぼろを出す means inadvertently exposing a hidden fault or one's true nature.
A clothing design becoming outdated is 古くなる, not ぼろになる in this sense.
Searching for others' faults is あらを探す, not ぼろを探す.

n2-set-5-q-30.translation: Choose the correct use of joutou: This is a very fine-quality item.
n2-set-5-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: 上等 - high quality or first-rate

choices.reason: 上等なお品 describes a fine-quality item and fits the polite sales expression.
Caring for an ill mother is admirable, but 上等だ does not normally praise that behavior.
A commendable way of thinking is 立派な考え, not usually 上等な考え.
Raising five children alone makes her admirable, 立派な女性, not 上等な女性.

n2-set-5-q-31.translation: Choose the correct use of discipline: He leads a disciplined life, almost like someone in the military.
n2-set-5-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: 規律正しい - disciplined or orderly

choices.reason: A busy practice session concerns its schedule or content, not its 規律.
規律正しい生活 means a disciplined, orderly way of life.
A bold decision that saved the firm is a 決断, not a 規律.
Limiting eligibility to experienced applicants takes 制限する, not 規律する.

n2-set-5-q-32.translation: Choose the correct use of imagination: She keeps daydreaming about marrying a millionaire.

choices.reason: For an unimaginable result one says 想像もつかなかった, not 空想もつかなかった.
A dream of becoming a star is 夢を見続ける; 空想を見る is not the usual pairing.
Making plans for future life takes 計画を立てる, not 空想を立てる.
空想ばかりしている describes repeatedly indulging in fantasies or daydreams.

n2-set-5-q-33.translation: My room is spacious and, on top of that, new and pleasant to be in.
n2-set-5-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: 上に - in addition; on top of that

choices.reason: ながらも means although and would imply contrast, not two favorable features.
かわりに means instead of or in exchange for, not adding a second benefit.
とはいえ means even so, a concession rather than cumulative praise.
上に adds another quality of the same positive kind: spacious and new.

n2-set-5-q-34.translation: Fine weather is expected nationwide from tomorrow through the weekend.
n2-set-5-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: から...にかけて - from...through, over a time span

choices.reason: に続いて means following something; it does not complete the range from tomorrow to the weekend.
にかけて pairs naturally with から to indicate a span of time or area.
に渡って means throughout an extent, but 明日から週末に渡って is not this range construction.
に及んで means reaching or extending to, not the normal から... range expression.

n2-set-5-q-35.translation: Even knowing it is wrong, people sometimes commit crimes; that is human nature.
n2-set-5-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: というものだ - that is simply how things are

choices.reason: ということだ reports a fact or conclusion; it does not express the speaker's general judgment here.
という人 would mean a person called that, not a judgment about humanity.
というものだ presents a general truth or natural judgment about human behavior.
というわけだ explains a logical consequence, not this broad statement of human nature.

n2-set-5-q-36.translation: Missing the lottery win by just one number is so frustrating I cannot stand it.
n2-set-5-q-36.correctAnswerEnglish: くやしくてならない - unbearably frustrating

choices.reason: てならない intensifies an involuntary feeling; the frustration is overwhelming.
なれない means cannot become; it does not intensify くやしい.
なるまい means probably will not become or resolves not to, not an uncontrollable feeling.
なりきれない means cannot fully become, not unbearable frustration.

n2-set-5-q-37.translation: A: You look pale. B: You see, I am so busy that I have no time to rest.
n2-set-5-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: なにしろ - you see; the fact is

choices.reason: なんとか means somehow or by some means, not introducing the reason for looking pale.
なんでも can mean apparently or anything, not this direct explanation of the speaker's state.
なにとぞ is a formal please used in requests, not a reason for exhaustion.
なにしろ introduces an emphatic reason: the speaker is extremely busy.

n2-set-5-q-38.translation: I was often sick as a child, but I have become completely healthy now.
n2-set-5-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: 病気がち - frequently prone to illness

choices.reason: 病気みたい means seeming ill, not having repeated illnesses in childhood.
病気がち means habitually prone to being sick; it contrasts with present good health.
病気っぽい means sickly-looking or somewhat ill, not the habitual condition marked by がち.
病気ぎみ means feeling slightly ill at a particular time, not repeatedly sick in childhood.

n2-set-5-q-39.translation: I initially disliked Japanese food, but as I kept eating it, I gradually came to like it.
n2-set-5-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: 食べるうちに - while continuing to eat it

choices.reason: 食べるうちに describes a gradual change occurring while repeatedly eating the food.
食べたうちに uses a completed past form where ongoing 食べるうちに is needed.
食べもしないで means without even eating it; that cannot explain growing to like it.
食べるそばから means immediately after each eating; it does not express gradual acclimatization.

n2-set-5-q-40.translation: I am good at Chinese. If you need an interpreter, please tell me anytime.
n2-set-5-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: おっしゃってください - please tell me, honorific

choices.reason: おっしゃる is the respectful form of 言う, appropriate for asking the listener to speak.
申す is humble for one's own speech; 申されて mixes it with an unsuitable honorific construction.
言われていただけますか combines passive and receiving forms unnaturally for this request.
申していただけますか wrongly uses the humble verb 申す for the listener's action.

n2-set-5-q-41.translation: He often says, 'I would not want to live long if it meant being bedridden,' but he makes a big fuss when he falls ill.
n2-set-5-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: 長生きをしたくないものだ - one would not want to live long

choices.reason: 長生きをしたいものだ expresses wanting longevity, contrary to 寝たきりになってまで.
長生きはするものだ states a general rule about living long, not his aversion to bedridden life.
長生きをしたくないものだ completes the idea that longevity is not worth being bedridden.
長生きはしないものだ makes an impersonal rule and lacks the wanted or unwanted feeling.

n2-set-5-q-42.translation: Although I have taken piano lessons continuously since childhood, I never became very good at it.
n2-set-5-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: あまりうまくならなかった - did not become very good

choices.reason: とてもうまくなった is a positive result, but ものの calls for a contrasting outcome.
あまりうまくならなかった contrasts with years of lessons, fitting the concessive ものの.
きっとうまくなるだろう predicts future success, not a disappointing result of past lessons.
うまくなるべきだ states an obligation, not what actually happened despite lessons.

n2-set-5-q-43.translation: The finest chef used the finest ingredients, so there is no way the food could taste bad.
n2-set-5-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: まずいわけがない - it cannot possibly taste bad

choices.reason: まずいわけではない merely says it is not necessarily bad, weaker than the stated grounds allow.
まずくないわけでもない leaves open that it might be bad, opposing the speaker's confidence.
まずいわけがない emphatically rules out bad taste because of the chef and ingredients.
まずくないわけにもいかない concerns an obligation not to be good; it is illogical here.

n2-set-5-q-44.translation: If you only voice an opinion about the school festival but do nothing, that does not count as participating.
n2-set-5-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: 参加することにはならない - does not amount to participating

choices.reason: することにはならない means the actions described do not qualify as actual participation.
することはならない omits the に required by ことにはならない.
したことにはなる says it does count as having participated, opposite to doing nothing.
したことになる likewise claims past participation, contrary to the condition.

n2-set-5-q-45.translation: Having grown up in America, her English pronunciation is beautiful, but her grammar is not correct.
n2-set-5-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: あって - completing アメリカ育ちだけあって, as expected from having grown up in America

choices.reason: 発音 is fourth: アメリカ育ちだけあって発音はきれいだが. It names what is beautiful.
だけ is second after アメリカ育ち; it joins あって to form だけあって.
アメリカ育ち is first and supplies the reason for her good pronunciation.
あって is third, at the star; full order is アメリカ育ち / だけ / あって / 発音.

n2-set-5-q-46.translation: Even when it is not my mistake, there are times when I have no choice but to apologize to a customer.
n2-set-5-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: あやまらざる - part of あやまらざるを得ない, must apologize

choices.reason: とき is fourth and forms ときもあります, there are also such times.
あやまらざる is second, at the star, and requires を得ない to express necessity.
お客様に is first; に marks the person to whom the apology is made.
を得ない is third and completes あやまらざるを得ない, having no alternative.

n2-set-5-q-47.translation: Even if I were to build a house, it would be somewhere far from the town center.
n2-set-5-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: と - completing 建てるとしても, even if I build

choices.reason: しても is third and joins と to complete としても, even if.
建てる is first after 家を; it is the verb for building a house.
と is second, at the star; full order is 建てる / と / しても / ずっと.
ずっと is fourth and intensifies 遠い, far away from the center.

n2-set-5-q-48.translation: The winning marathon runner reportedly never skips practice, even on rainy days, unless a typhoon comes.
n2-set-5-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: 限り - unless, in 来ない限り

choices.reason: 限り is third, at the star, completing 台風でも来ない限り, unless a typhoon comes.
雨の日 is fourth and joins も, even on rainy days.
来ない is second and modifies 限り to state the exception.
台風でも is first; it sets up the exceptional weather condition.

n2-set-5-q-49.translation: The autumn rice and fruit harvest depends on the summer weather.
n2-set-5-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: 夏の天気 - summer weather, the condition on which the harvest depends

choices.reason: 収穫量は is second and makes harvest volume the topic of the sentence.
次第 is fourth; 夏の天気次第 means depending on summer weather.
秋の is first and modifies 収穫量, the autumn harvest volume.
夏の天気 is third, at the star; full order is 秋の / 収穫量は / 夏の天気 / 次第.

n2-set-5-q-50.translation: There is something abnormal about the heat of recent Japanese summers.
n2-set-5-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: ものがあります - there is a noticeable quality of something

choices.reason: ことがあります means something sometimes occurs; 異常なことがあります would shift the claim to occasional events.
ものがあります expresses the speaker's strong impression: the heat has an abnormal quality.
わけです gives a logical conclusion, not an impression after 異常な.
ところです means being at a point or stage, not the abnormal nature of the heat.

n2-set-5-q-51.translation: Air conditioning used to be said to be bad for the body, but now not using it can even put your life in danger.
n2-set-5-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: 危ないほどです - to the extent that one's life is at risk

choices.reason: 危ないばかりです means only dangerous and does not express the extreme degree meant here.
危ないはずです means it should be dangerous, a conjecture rather than the passage's warning.
危ないほどです states that the heat is so severe that life can be endangered.
危ないところです describes narrowly escaping danger, not the ongoing summer conditions.

n2-set-5-q-52.translation: Because air conditioners expel hot air and prevent the ground from cooling at night, using them can make summer even hotter.
n2-set-5-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: 暑くしている - is making it hotter

choices.reason: 過ごしやすくする means making summer easier to endure, but the paragraph stresses expelled heat.
暑くしている says air conditioners themselves contribute to hotter summers outside.
涼しくする describes cooling indoor air, not the warming outdoor effect explained here.
快適にする means making comfortable and ignores the heat retained outside at night.

n2-set-5-q-53.translation: When air passes between wet leaves, it removes more heat than when it passes between dry leaves, lowering the air temperature.
n2-set-5-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: a ぬれた / b かわいた - wet leaves versus dry leaves

choices.reason: Wet leaves first and dry leaves second match the passage's evaporation-based cooling comparison.
Dry leaves first and wet leaves second reverse the comparison; the wet leaves remove more heat.
